lines: The race now rides through its world: the road, the terrain and the sky of the map you chose.
The camera sits at your place on the route and moves forward at your virtual speed. Three seconds on, Old Town's cobbles have rolled by.
Each map draws its own world: Neon Docklands after dark, Vice City's beachfront, the prairie's wind farm and the Dolomites' valley.
Pause a solo race, and the world holds still with it, frame for frame.
Every scene is main's, copied as it is: the renderer, the road and its bends, the shared kit, and a module for each world, with their unit tests.
From a phone to a desktop, the world fills the screen behind the panels, never stretched.
What the tests prove: the world moves as you ride and holds when you pause, main's unit tests pass here, and the first download is unchanged.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
